newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes quiet as players assess diffs.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes quiet as players assess diffs.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes were inactive early Monday, with traders studying the market after a major drop in Alaskan differentials late Friday.
West Coast spot traders said Exxon sold a 400,000 barrel cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at $1.32 off West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Friday.
The discount for ANS stands 0.27 cents a barrel lower than the previous deal done April 4, putting outright prices at $18.43/18.63 a barrel Monday.
Heavy imports of South American crude for May have undercut the price of competing ANS, now offered at $0.95 cents a barrel, buyers claimed.
"Everyone said the market was talked to high," one refinery buyer said, referring to the offer price.
Texaco is expecting another load of Colombian South Blend, an ANS substitute, to be delivered to its Washington state refinery, May 20, traders said.
ARCO on Monday looked to buy Wilmington (THUMS) crude oil for May, after traders said the company's production fell short of supply obligations.
Line 63 and California heavy crude markets remained well- supplied, with no deals reported early.
